clinicalPearls: Caused by deficiency of aspartylglucosaminidase (glycosylasparaginase), which cleaves the linkage between the oligosaccharide and asparagine in glycoprotein degradation
Notably enriched in the Finnish population as part of the Finnish disease heritage, though it occurs worldwide
Follows a characteristic course: relatively normal early infancy, then slowly progressive intellectual decline through childhood into adulthood
Coarse facies, connective tissue laxity, recurrent infections, and mild skeletal changes are typical, with behavioural problems emerging over time
Adult patients often show a plateau followed by earlier-than-normal decline, sometimes with psychiatric features
Urinary oligosaccharide screening detects aspartylglucosamine, the accumulated glycoasparagine
Diagnosis is confirmed by deficient aspartylglucosaminidase activity and AGA gene testing
reference.pathophysiology: Aspartylglucosaminuria is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in AGA, encoding the lysosomal enzyme aspartylglucosaminidase (glycosylasparaginase). This enzyme hydrolyses the bond between N-acetylglucosamine and asparagine, a late step in the degradation of N-linked glycoproteins. Its deficiency causes accumulation of aspartylglucosamine and related glycoasparagines within lysosomes across many tissues, with excretion of aspartylglucosamine in the urine. Progressive storage in the central nervous system underlies the characteristically slow intellectual decline, while systemic accumulation contributes to the coarse features, connective tissue laxity, and skeletal changes. A single founder variant accounts for most Finnish cases. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Other oligosaccharidoses such as alpha-mannosidosis and fucosidosis
Mucopolysaccharidoses with coarse facies and slow cognitive decline
Sanfilippo syndrome given the behavioural and cognitive course
Other lysosomal storage disorders with adult psychiatric presentations
additionalInvestigations: Leucocyte or fibroblast aspartylglucosaminidase enzyme assay
AGA gene sequencing, including testing for the Finnish founder variant where relevant
Brain MRI for white matter and atrophic changes
Developmental and neuropsychological assessment to track decline
redFlags: Progressive intellectual decline after relatively normal early development
Emerging psychiatric or behavioural disturbance in adolescence or adulthood
reference.prognosis: The disorder is slowly progressive, with many patients reaching adulthood before a phase of more rapid cognitive decline; life expectancy is reduced but survival into middle adulthood is common. Management is supportive, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation has been explored in selected cases.
pitfalls: Attributing the slow cognitive decline to a static intellectual disability and missing the progressive storage disorder
Screening only for glycosaminoglycans and missing the oligosaccharide pattern
Overlooking the diagnosis outside the Finnish population where it also occurs
Failing to consider it in adults presenting with new psychiatric symptoms and intellectual disability
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Supportive and rehabilitative care with special education plus speech, occupational and physiotherapy to support development and function
Management of the behavioural and psychiatric symptoms that emerge over time with appropriate psychotropic therapy and behavioural support
Prompt treatment of the recurrent infections characteristic of the disorder
Orthopaedic and dental surveillance for skeletal dysostosis and the effects of connective-tissue laxity
Consideration of haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in carefully selected early cases, where it has been explored as a disease-modifying option
Multidisciplinary metabolic follow-up tracking the slowly progressive cognitive decline with serial neuropsychological assessment
Genetic counselling and family screening for this autosomal recessive condition, including testing for the Finnish founder variant where relevant
